2026-06-16T11:44:45.3985486Z 
2026-06-16T11:44:45.3985595Z     def wait(self, timeout=None):
2026-06-16T11:44:45.3985909Z         """Wait until notified or until a timeout occurs.
2026-06-16T11:44:45.3986215Z     
2026-06-16T11:44:45.3986509Z         If the calling thread has not acquired the lock when this method is
2026-06-16T11:44:45.3986915Z         called, a RuntimeError is raised.
2026-06-16T11:44:45.3987187Z     
2026-06-16T11:44:45.3987493Z         This method releases the underlying lock, and then blocks until it is
2026-06-16T11:44:45.3987986Z         awakened by a notify() or notify_all() call for the same condition
2026-06-16T11:44:45.3988606Z         variable in another thread, or until the optional timeout occurs. Once
2026-06-16T11:44:45.3989077Z         awakened or timed out, it re-acquires the lock and returns.
2026-06-16T11:44:45.3989419Z     
2026-06-16T11:44:45.3989705Z         When the timeout argument is present and not None, it should be a
2026-06-16T11:44:45.3990205Z         floating-point number specifying a timeout for the operation in seconds
2026-06-16T11:44:45.3990624Z         (or fractions thereof).
2026-06-16T11:44:45.3991028Z     
2026-06-16T11:44:45.3991328Z         When the underlying lock is an RLock, it is not released using its
2026-06-16T11:44:45.3991809Z         release() method, since this may not actually unlock the lock when it
2026-06-16T11:44:45.3992316Z         was acquired multiple times recursively. Instead, an internal interface
2026-06-16T11:44:45.3992806Z         of the RLock class is used, which really unlocks it even when it has
2026-06-16T11:44:45.3993307Z         been recursively acquired several times. Another internal interface is
2026-06-16T11:44:45.3993817Z         then used to restore the recursion level when the lock is reacquired.
2026-06-16T11:44:45.3994188Z     
2026-06-16T11:44:45.3994380Z         """
2026-06-16T11:44:45.3994598Z         if not self._is_owned():
2026-06-16T11:44:45.3994930Z             raise RuntimeError("cannot wait on un-acquired lock")
2026-06-16T11:44:45.3995281Z         waiter = _allocate_lock()

2026-06-16T11:44:45.4113523Z     def wait(self, timeout=None):
2026-06-16T11:44:45.4113836Z         """Wait until notified or until a timeout occurs.
2026-06-16T11:44:45.4114142Z     
2026-06-16T11:44:45.4114446Z         If the calling thread has not acquired the lock when this method is
2026-06-16T11:44:45.4114844Z         called, a RuntimeError is raised.
2026-06-16T11:44:45.4115117Z     
2026-06-16T11:44:45.4115423Z         This method releases the underlying lock, and then blocks until it is
2026-06-16T11:44:45.4115909Z         awakened by a notify() or notify_all() call for the same condition
2026-06-16T11:44:45.4116387Z         variable in another thread, or until the optional timeout occurs. Once
2026-06-16T11:44:45.4116855Z         awakened or timed out, it re-acquires the lock and returns.
2026-06-16T11:44:45.4117215Z

2026-06-16T11:44:45.4118001Z         floating-point number specifying a timeout for the operation in seconds

2026-06-16T11:44:45.4308535Z         release() method, since this may not actually unlock the lock when it
2026-06-16T11:44:45.4309170Z         was acquired multiple times recursively. Instead, an internal interface
2026-06-16T11:44:45.4309666Z         of the RLock class is used, which really unlocks it even when it has
2026-06-16T11:44:45.4310163Z         been recursively acquired several times. Another internal interface is
